papers.title_in_file: A Study of Entanglement and Ansatz Expressivity for the Transverse-Field Ising Model using Variational Quantum Eigensolver
papers.what_it_is: A short proceedings paper comparing three VQE ansatzes (HEA, HVA, HVA-SB) on the transverse-field Ising model in one to three dimensions by exact simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that VQE systematically underestimates entanglement, reflecting the difficulty of capturing highly correlated states with shallow circuits.
quotes: it systematically underestimates entanglement, reflecting the difficulty of capturing highly correlated states with shallow circuits
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation study; stated in Section 2, p.5.
assertions.reader_inference: The statement is made for shallow circuits and the 3D real-amplitude ansatz; the paper gives no scaling law.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulations are exact state-vector runs reaching up to 15 qubits in 1D, with HEA optimized by L-BFGS and the HVA variants by COBYLA.
quotes: enabling systems of up to 15 qubits in 1D
HEA is optimized using the L-BFGS algorithm, whereas the more rugged landscapes of HVA and SB are handled with the derivative-free COBYLA optimizer
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation setup in Section 2, p.4.

assertions.value: The authors report that increasing the number of layers gives only a gradual improvement for HEA, whereas HVA and HVA-SB show a sudden transition from poor to accurate ground-state energy estimation.
quotes: increasing the number of layers leads to only a gradual improvement in HEA, whereas both HVA and HVA-SB show a sudden transition from poor to accurate ground-state energy estimation
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study of 1D and 2D TFIM; Section 4, p.8.

assertions.value: The authors state that expressivity and optimization stability are competing requirements in VQE, and that in higher-dimensional simulations the optimization becomes more challenging.
quotes: our results show that expressivity and optimization stability are competing
In higher-dimensional simulations, the increased interaction connectivity and stronger entanglement make the optimization more challenging.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author conclusion from one empirical study, Section 4, p.8.

papers.title_in_file: A Multiclass Quantum Aligned Centroid Kernel
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Related Work, Background 2.1-2.2, Results (4, trainability and real-world benchmark parts), Conclusion, Limitations; appendices not read.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes McQuack, a trainable quantum kernel method for multiclass problems with linear scaling in training set size, benchmarked in simulation and on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the quantum neural network family of the QML Benchmark Suite in simulation McQuack consistently outperforms existing pure quantum models, and is the second best quantum model, behind a classifier that uses classical neural networks for pre- and postprocessing.
quotes: benchmarking against the quantum neural network family of the QML Benchmark Suite demonstrated that McQuack consistently outperforms existing
McQuack is the second best quantum model, being only outperformed by the DressedQuantumCircuitClassifier, which uses classical neural nets for pre- and postprocessing.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark from one study (noiseless simulation).
assertions.reader_inference: The classical MLPClassifier ranked above all quantum models in the same benchmark.

assertions.value: The authors report that evaluating the untrained model on 124 qubits across two IBM systems revealed no statistically significant difference in accuracy relative to the baselines.
quotes: evaluating the untrained model on 124 qubits across two IBM systems revealed no statistically significant difference in accuracy relative to the baselines
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result from one study, untrained model only; Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors report no evidence of barren plateaus up to 13 qubits.
quotes: Overall, we observe no evidence of barren plateaus up to 13 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result limited to 13 qubits; Section 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that training on quantum hardware is currently infeasible for practically relevant system sizes, so hardware experiments are restricted to untrained models; that the simulations are noiseless; and that McQuack does not outperform simple classical baselines like feedforward neural networks.
quotes: training on quantum hardware is currently infeasible for practically relevant system sizes due to the high cost of gradient estimation via the parameter-shift rule
the simulations are performed on a noiseless simulator, which may overestimate performance compared to noisy hardware
it does not outperform simple classical baselines like feedforward neural networks
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors list these as limitations in Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: Towards Automated Selection of Quantum Encoding Circuits via Meta-Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 2, 3.1-3.3, Section 4 (text, not all tables), Section 5, Appendix A-C headings; tables read only in part.
papers.what_it_is: A meta-learning recommender that predicts which of nine quantum-kernel encoding circuits suits a dataset from 24 classical complexity metrics, with no quantum evaluation at inference.

assertions.value: The authors report Top-3 accuracy of up to 85.7% in identifying the best-performing encoding circuit among nine candidates.
quotes: Both approaches achieve Top-3 accuracy of up to 85.7% in identifying the
Nine candidates are assessed alongside 24 classical complexity metrics serving as features
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on a small meta-dataset.
assertions.reader_inference: The 85.7% figure is 6 of 7 held-out datasets per Table 5 (a table figure, not in the quotes); a one-dataset change moves it by about 14 points.

assertions.value: The authors state that the meta-dataset is built from 200 binary classification datasets, 174 synthetic and 26 real-world.
quotes: The meta-dataset is constructed from 200 binary classification datasets, comprising 174 synthetic and 26 real-world datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own dataset setup in Section 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that the framework achieves Top-3 accuracy of up to 85.7% while reducing computational cost up to 78% compared to exhaustive quantum evaluation.
quotes: 85.7% on the meta-dataset while reducing computational cost up to 78% compared to exhaustive quantum evaluation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Contribution statement; the derivation of the 78% figure was not located in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors state that scaling the meta-dataset beyond 200 instances and evaluating under noise models are additional directions to strengthen generalization and practical applicability.
quotes: Scaling the meta-dataset beyond 200 instances and evaluating under noise models are additional directions to strengthen generalization and practical applicability.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors name these as open directions in Section 5, p.14.

papers.title_in_file: Separating Ansatz Discovery from Deployment on Larger Problems: Reinforcement Learning for Modular Circuit Design
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Background 2.1, Conclusions; Sections 3-5 (methods and results) and appendices not read in full.
papers.what_it_is: Reinforcement learning (RLVQC) learns a reusable two-qubit block on small instances that is composed into QAOA-style ansatzes for larger QUBO instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that blocks discovered on n = 8 instances remain effective when deployed on larger instances (n = 12 and n = 16).
quotes: n = 8 instances remain effective when deployed on larger instances (n = 12 and n = 16), supporting the feasibility of reusing learned modular structure across problem sizes.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations on QUBO instances up to n = 16.
assertions.reader_inference: The largest size tested is n = 16, which classical methods handle easily.

assertions.value: The authors report that RLVQC Block consistently achieves higher approximation ratios than RLVQC Global across Maximum Cut and Minimum Vertex Cover instances, while it is less competitive under Maximum Clique.
quotes: RLVQC Block consistently achieves higher approximation ratios than RLVQC Global across Maximum Cut and Minimum Vertex Cover instances, while is less competitive under Maximum Clique
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; Section 6.

assertions.value: The authors report that the circuits discovered by both RL variants frequently use substantially fewer CX gates than standard QAOA while maintaining competitive solution quality.
quotes: the circuits discovered by both RL variants frequently use substantially fewer CX gates than standard QAOA, which is desirable in view of hardware constraints and noise sensitivity, while maintaining competitive solution quality
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; Section 6.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not aim to establish a new state-of-the-art solver or a computational advantage over classical methods.
quotes: While we do not aim to establish a new state-of-the-art solver or a computational advantage over classical methods
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract, p.2.

papers.title_in_file: Geometric quantum machine learning of BQPA protocols and latent graph classifiers
papers.what_it_is: A letter that casts Simon's problem as unsupervised circuit classification and shows a geometric QML workflow with an equivariant feature map that recovers Simon's algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numerical test uses a system size N = 6 with M = 120 unique functions, half of them 1:1, measured with a fixed number of shots, Ns = 5000.
quotes: Choosing a system size N = 6, we generate a dataset
with M = 120 unique functions, ensuring that half of the functions are 1:1
using a fixed number of shots, Ns = 5000
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own simulation setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that kernel PCA and k-means clustering of the measured features show a clear separation between the two classes of Boolean functions.
quotes: the separation between the two classes of functions is clear, showing the success of this hybrid quantum-classical procedure
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one simulation at N = 6; Fig. 3.
assertions.reader_inference: The test is a simulation at six bits; it does not demonstrate scaling.

assertions.value: The authors state that using a group-equivariant version enhanced by symmetries they effectively rediscovered Simon's algorithm for analyzing Boolean functions.
quotes: Using its group-equivariant version enhanced by symmetries, we effectively rediscovered Simon's algorithm for analyzing Boolean functions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' summary conclusion; the protocol is derived and simulated in the paper.
assertions.reader_inference: Simon's algorithm is already known, so this is a re-derivation of a known separation, not new advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the utility of the provided example remains limited due to the black-box operation inherent to Simon's algorithm, and conjecture that there may be problems that avoid this regime yet enjoy the exponential speed-up.
quotes: While the utility of the provided example remains limited due to black-box operation inherent to Simon's algorithm, we conjecture that there may be problems that avoid this regime yet enjoy the exponential speed-up, conditioned on properties of the data.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit in the introduction.

papers.title_in_file: Variational quantum algorithms for local Hamiltonian problems (dissertation, Skolkovo Institute of Science and Technology)
papers.partial_detail: Contents, Introduction, Chapter 3 discussion (3.4), Chapter 4 introduction, Theorem 5.3.1 and 5.4.1 statements, 5.6 Discussion, Conclusions; proofs and chapter 6 not read.
papers.what_it_is: A PhD thesis on VQE for physical models, quantum classifiers for quantum data, barren plateaus with a gradient-variance lower bound, and GHZ-state fidelity bounds.

assertions.value: The thesis reports that the scaling of the error with circuit depth was close to exponential in all models studied, and that states near the phase transition point are the hardest to approximate with a variational circuit.
quotes: In all models, the scaling of the error with circuit depth was close to exponential, agreeing with existing literature.
The states near the phase transition point are the hardest to approximate with a variational circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical results on small spin and Hubbard models; Conclusions.

assertions.value: The thesis proves a lower bound on the variance of cost function derivatives for ansatzes whose blocks are independently parametrized local 2-designs; the bound depends on the size of the causal cones of the operators in the cost function Hamiltonian and on the position of the gate in the circuit.
quotes: Let each block of the ansatz be an independently parametrized local 2-design.

We derived a lower bound on the variance of cost function derivatives in variational quantum circuits. The bound mainly depends on two things: the size of the causal cones of the operators in the cost function Hamiltonian, and the position of the gate in the circuit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 5.4.1, p.92.

assertions.value: The thesis reports that the barren plateau effect for short-depth circuits sets in at a different pace depending on the fermion-to-qubit encoding: derivatives vanish essentially immediately for the Jordan-Wigner transform and more gradually for the Bravyi-Kitaev transform.
quotes: The barren plateaus effect for short-depth circuits sets on at a different pace depending on the choice of the fermion-to-qubit encoding. In particular, the derivatives vanish essentially immediately for the Jordan-Wigner transform and more gradually for the Bravyi-Kitaev transform.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result on a Hubbard-type model; Conclusions.

assertions.value: The thesis states that the experiments with the Hubbard model hint that the fast convergence of energy error with circuit depth may just be a consequence of a small number of qubits.
quotes: the experiments with the Hubbard model hint that this may just be the consequence of a small number of qubits
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limit in Section 3.4, p.67.

papers.title_in_file: Entangling Machine Learning with Quantum Tensor Networks
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, results discussion on parameter counts and valid-fraction robustness, Conclusion, Limitations; theory sections and appendix tables skimmed only.
papers.what_it_is: A classical study of matrix product state and factored-core MPS models for classifying and modeling Motzkin spin chains, as a language-modeling proxy, against an MLP baseline.

assertions.value: The authors report that the tensor models reach near perfect classifying ability and maintain a stable level of performance as the number of valid training examples is decreased.
quotes: We find that the tensor models reach near perfect classifying ability, and maintain a stable level of performance as the number of valid training examples is decreased.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one toy dataset; abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: The models run on classical hardware; no quantum computer is involved, so the quantum label is an inspiration, not a resource.

assertions.value: The authors report that at the smallest valid-chain fraction tested the tensor models barely do better than a random classifier, and that the neural baseline pulls ahead there.
quotes: the tensor models barely do better than a random classifier
This is the regime where our neural baseline pulls ahead, suggesting that neither model-type is a clear winner.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one toy dataset; Conclusion.

assertions.value: The authors report that the tensor models perform significantly better with smaller batch sizes, to the point of being unable to learn at all with large batch sizes.
quotes: that they perform significantly better with smaller batch sizes, instead of larger ones (to the point of the models' inability to learn at all with large batch sizes)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation; cause not explained by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that limits on time led to the use of a smaller, toy dataset and that all models had to be built from scratch.
quotes: the limitations in time also led to the decision to use a smaller, toy dataset
all models had to be built from scratch
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Limitations section.

papers.title_in_file: Variational decision diagrams for quantum-inspired machine learning applications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections IV-V (trainability and ground-state experiments), VI discussion, VII Conclusions; Section II definitions skimmed; appendices not read.
papers.what_it_is: Introduces variational decision diagrams (VDDs), a quantum-inspired classical ansatz, and tests their trainability and ground-state estimation on Ising and Heisenberg Hamiltonians.

assertions.value: The authors report that the gradient variance of the VDD accordion ansatz does not decay exponentially fast with the number of qubits, so it does not show the barren plateau phenomenon for the Hamiltonians under consideration.
quotes: it does not decay exponentially fast with respect to the number of qubits. Thus, the accordion ansatz does not show the barren plateau phenomenon for the Hamiltonians under consideration
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one numerical study at small qubit counts; Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the calculations involve a small number of qubits (on the order of 10 qubits) using the whole state vector, and that the results hold for the accordion ansatz while other DD structures may have different trainability properties.
quotes: the required calculations to show our findings involve a small number of qubits (on the order of 10 qubits), we rely on building the whole state vector
results in this section are valid for this ansatz, and other DD structures may have different trainability properties
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this scope in Section IV.

assertions.value: The authors state that the accordion ansatz struggles to capture subtle state structures in certain regimes, such as moderate transverse fields in the disordered phase of the TFIM.
quotes: it struggles to capture subtle state structures in certain regimes, such as moderate transverse fields in the disordered phase of the TFIM
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated limitation in Section VII.
